sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ mahatā javena; śikhaṇḍinaṃ bhīṣmam abhidravantam āvārayām āsa hi śalya enaṃ; śastreṇa ghoreṇa sudurjayena
english: As Śikhaṇḍin rushed with great speed against Bhīṣma, charging upon him, Śalya checked him with a terrible and well-nigh invincible weapon.

sanskrit: sa cāpi dṛṣṭvā samudīryamāṇam; astraṃ yugāntāgnisamaprabhāvam nāsau vyamuhyad drupadasya putro; rājan mahendrapratimaprabhāvaḥ
english: And though he saw that weapon hurled at him, blazing with a power like the fire at the end of an age, the son of Drupada was not bewildered, O king, for his splendor was the equal of great Indra's.

sanskrit: tasthau ca tatraiva mahādhanuṣmāñ; śarais tad astraṃ pratibādhamānaḥ athādade vāruṇam anyad astraṃ; śikhaṇḍy athograṃ pratighātāya tasya tad astram astreṇa vidāryamāṇaṃ; khasthāḥ surā dadṛśuḥ pārthivāś ca
english: That mighty bowman stood his ground there, beating back the weapon with his arrows; then Śikhaṇḍin took up another fierce weapon, the Vāruṇa, to counter it. The gods stationed in the sky and the kings below beheld that weapon shattered by his weapon.

sanskrit: bhīṣmas tu rājan samare mahātmā; dhanuḥ sucitraṃ dhvajam eva cāpi chittvānadat pāṇḍusutasya vīro; yudhiṣṭhirasyājamīḍhasya rājñaḥ
english: But great-souled Bhīṣma, that hero, having in the battle cut off the splendidly wrought bow and the banner of Pāṇḍu's son, King Yudhiṣṭhira of Ajamīḍha's line, raised a war cry, O king.

sanskrit: tataḥ samutsṛjya dhanuḥ sabāṇaṃ; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ vīkṣya bhayābhibhūtam gadāṃ pragṛhyābhipapāta saṃkhye; jayadrathaṃ bhīmasenaḥ padātiḥ
english: Then, casting aside his bow with its arrows and seeing Yudhiṣṭhira overcome with fear, Bhīmasena seized his mace and on foot fell upon Jayadratha in the fray.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ mahatā javena; jayadrathaḥ sagadaṃ bhīmasenam vivyādha ghorair yamadaṇḍakalpaiḥ; śitaiḥ śaraiḥ pañcaśataiḥ samantāt
english: As Bhīmasena rushed upon him at great speed, mace in hand, Jayadratha pierced him on every side with five hundred dreadful, whetted arrows that were like the rod of Yama.

sanskrit: acintayitvā sa śarāṃs tarasvī; vṛkodaraḥ krodhaparītacetāḥ jaghāna vāhān samare samastān; āraṭṭajān sindhurājasya saṃkhye
english: Heeding not those arrows, the impetuous Vṛkodara, his mind seized by wrath, slew in the battle all the Āraṭṭa-born steeds of the king of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: tato 'bhivīkṣyāpratimaprabhāvas; tavātmajas tvaramāṇo rathena abhyāyayau bhīmasenaṃ nihantuṃ; samudyatāstraḥ surarājakalpaḥ
english: Then your son of matchless power, beholding this, came hurrying on his chariot to slay Bhīmasena, his weapon upraised, like the king of the gods himself.

sanskrit: bhīmo 'py athainaṃ sahasā vinadya; pratyudyayau gadayā tarjamānaḥ samudyatāṃ tāṃ yamadaṇḍakalpāṃ; dṛṣṭvā gadāṃ te kuravaḥ samantāt
english: And Bhīma too, roaring aloud all at once, advanced against him, brandishing his mace in menace; and seeing that mace upraised like the rod of Yama, your Kurus on every side...

sanskrit: vihāya sarve tava putram ugraṃ; pātaṃ gadāyāḥ parihartukāmāḥ apakrāntās tumule saṃvimarde; sudāruṇe bhārata mohanīye
english: ...all of them abandoned your fierce son, wishing to avoid the descent of that mace, and fell back amid the tumultuous, most dreadful and bewildering crush of battle, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: amūḍhacetās tv atha citraseno; mahāgadām āpatantīṃ nirīkṣya rathaṃ samutsṛjya padātir ājau; pragṛhya khaḍgaṃ vimalaṃ ca carma avaplutaḥ siṃha ivācalāgrāj; jagāma cānyaṃ bhuvi bhūmideśam
english: But Citrasena, his mind undismayed, watching the great mace come hurtling on, abandoned his chariot and on foot in the battle, seizing his bright sword and shield, leapt down like a lion from a mountain peak and made his way to another spot upon the ground.

sanskrit: gadāpi sā prāpya rathaṃ sucitraṃ; sāśvaṃ sasūtaṃ vinihatya saṃkhye jagāma bhūmiṃ jvalitā maholkā; bhraṣṭāmbarād gām iva saṃpatantī
english: And that mace, reaching the splendid chariot, smashed it utterly in the fray together with its horses and driver, and fell blazing to the earth, like a great meteor falling from the fallen sky to the ground.

sanskrit: āścaryabhūtaṃ sumahat tvadīyā; dṛṣṭvaiva tad bhārata saṃprahṛṣṭāḥ sarve vineduḥ sahitāḥ samantāt; pupūjire tava putraṃ sasainyāḥ
english: Seeing that exceedingly great marvel, your men, O Bhārata, were filled with delight, and all together raised a shout on every side, and with their troops honored your son.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca virathaṃ taṃ samāsādya citrasenaṃ manasvinam ratham āropayām āsa vikarṇas tanayas tava
english: Saṃjaya said: Coming up to that high-spirited Citrasena, now bereft of his chariot, your son Vikarṇa took him up onto his own car.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne tumule saṃkule bhṛśam bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavas tūrṇaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram upādravat
english: While that turmoil thus raged, exceedingly confused, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu swiftly rushed upon Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarathanāgāśvāḥ samakampanta sṛñjayāḥ mṛtyor āsyam anuprāptaṃ menire ca yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Then the Sṛñjayas trembled, with their chariots, elephants, and horses, and they thought Yudhiṣṭhira had passed into the very jaws of death.

sanskrit: yidhiṣṭhiro 'pi kauravyo yamābhyāṃ sahitaḥ prabhuḥ maheṣvāsaṃ naravyāghraṃ bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ yayau
english: But Yudhiṣṭhira too, the Kaurava lord, joined by the twins, advanced against the great bowman, that tiger among men, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi pramuñcan pāṇḍavo yudhi bhīṣmaṃ saṃchādayām āsa yathā megho divākaram
english: Then the son of Pāṇḍu, loosing thousands of arrows in the battle, covered Bhīṣma over as a cloud covers the sun.

sanskrit: tena samyak praṇītāni śarajālāni bhārata patijagrāha gāṅgeyaḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Those nets of arrows, well aimed by him, O Bhārata, the son of Gaṅgā received by the hundreds and by the thousands.

sanskrit: tathaiva śarajālāni bhīṣmeṇāstāni māriṣa ākāśe samadṛśyanta khagamānāṃ vrajā iva
english: And likewise the nets of arrows shot by Bhīṣma, O sire, appeared in the sky like flights of moving birds.

sanskrit: nimeṣārdhāc ca kaunteyaṃ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo yudhi adṛśyaṃ samare cakre śarajālena bhāgaśaḥ
english: And in half the blink of an eye Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu made the son of Kuntī invisible in the battle, piece by piece, with his net of arrows.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā kauravyasya mahātmanaḥ nārācaṃ preṣayām āsa kruddha āśīviṣopamam
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira in his wrath sent against the great-souled Kaurava an iron shaft like a venomous serpent.

sanskrit: asaṃprāptaṃ tatas taṃ tu kṣurapreṇa mahārathaḥ ciccheda samare rājan bhīṣmas tasya dhanuścyutam
english: But before it could reach him, that mighty car-warrior Bhīṣma, O king, cut that shaft, sped from his bow, with a razor-edged arrow in the battle.

sanskrit: taṃ tu chittvā raṇe bhīṣmo nārācaṃ kālasaṃmitam nijaghne kauravendrasya hayān kāñcanabhūṣaṇān
english: And having cut that iron shaft, fit to measure with death itself, Bhīṣma in the battle slew the gold-caparisoned horses of the Kaurava lord.

sanskrit: hatāśvaṃ tu rathaṃ tyaktvā dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ nakulasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then, abandoning the chariot whose horses were slain, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma swiftly mounted the chariot of great-souled Nakula.

sanskrit: yamāv api susaṃkruddhaḥ samāsādya raṇe tadā śaraiḥ saṃchādayām āsa bhīṣmaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Then, much enraged, Bhīṣma the conqueror of hostile cities closed in upon the twins as well in the battle and covered them over with his arrows.

sanskrit: tau tu dṛṣṭvā mahārāja bhīṣmabāṇaprapīḍitau jagāmātha parāṃ cintāṃ bhīṣmasya vadhakāṅkṣayā
english: Seeing those two, O great king, sorely afflicted by Bhīṣma's arrows, Yudhiṣṭhira fell into the deepest anxiety, longing for Bhīṣma's death.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro vaśyān rājñas tān samacodayat bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ sarve nihateti suhṛdgaṇān
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira urged on those obedient kings, his band of allies: "Let all of you together slay Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu!"

sanskrit: tatas te pārthivāḥ sarve śrutvā pārthasya bhāṣitam mahatā rathavaṃśena parivavruḥ pitāmaham
english: Then all those kings, hearing the word of Pārtha, surrounded the grandsire with a great host of chariots.

sanskrit: sa samantāt parivṛtaḥ pitā devavratas tava cikrīda dhanuṣā rājan pātayāno mahārathān
english: Surrounded on every side, your father Devavrata sported with his bow, O king, bringing down mighty car-warriors.

sanskrit: taṃ carantaṃ raṇe pārthā dadṛśuḥ kauravaṃ yudhi mṛgamadhyaṃ praviśyeva yathā siṃhaśiśuṃ vane
english: The sons of Pṛthā watched that Kaurava ranging through the battle as one might watch a lion's cub in the forest entering amid a herd of deer.

sanskrit: tarjayānaṃ raṇe śūrāṃs trāsayānaṃ ca sāyakaiḥ dṛṣṭvā tresur mahārāja siṃhaṃ mṛgagaṇā iva
english: Seeing him menace the brave in battle and terrify them with his arrows, they trembled, O great king, as herds of deer tremble before a lion.

sanskrit: raṇe bharatasiṃhasya dadṛśuḥ kṣatriyā gatim agner vāyusahāyasya yathā kakṣaṃ didhakṣataḥ
english: The warriors beheld the course of that lion of the Bhāratas in the battle, like the course of fire aided by the wind, eager to burn the dry brushwood.

sanskrit: śirāṃsi rathināṃ bhīṣmaḥ pātayām āsa saṃyuge tālebhya iva pakvāni phalāni kuśalo naraḥ
english: Bhīṣma struck down the heads of the chariot-warriors in the battle, as a skilled man brings down ripe fruits from the palm trees.

sanskrit: patadbhiś ca mahārāja śirobhir dharaṇītale babhūva tumulaḥ śabdaḥ patatām aśmanām iva
english: And with the heads falling to the surface of the earth, O great king, there arose a tumultuous din, like that of falling stones.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu tumule yuddhe vartamāne sudāruṇe sarveṣām eva sainyānām āsīd vyatikaro mahān
english: As that tumultuous and most dreadful battle raged on, there came a great confounding together of all the armies.

sanskrit: bhinneṣu teṣu vyūheṣu kṣatriyā itaretaram ekam ekaṃ samāhūya yuddhāyaivopatasthire
english: When those battle-arrays were broken, the warriors, calling out one to another, man against man, took their stand for combat.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu samāsādya bharatānāṃ pitāmaham abhidudrāva vegena tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: But Śikhaṇḍin, coming up to the grandsire of the Bhāratas, rushed at him with speed and cried, "Stand, stand!"

sanskrit: anādṛtya tato bhīṣmas taṃ śikhaṇḍinam āhave prayayau sṛñjayān kruddhaḥ strītvaṃ cintya śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: But Bhīṣma, disregarding that Śikhaṇḍin in the battle, mindful of Śikhaṇḍin's womanhood, advanced in wrath against the Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: sṛñjayās tu tato hṛṣṭā dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmaṃ mahāratham siṃhanādān bahuvidhāṃś cakruḥ śaṅkhavimiśritān
english: Then the Sṛñjayas, glad at seeing the mighty car-warrior Bhīṣma, raised lion-roars of many kinds, mingled with the blare of conches.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ vyatiṣaktarathadvipam aparāṃ diśam āsthāya sthite savitari prabho
english: Then the battle raged on, chariots and elephants entangled together, as the sun, O lord, took its place declining toward the western quarter.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno 'tha pāñcālyaḥ sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ pīḍayantau bhṛśaṃ sainyaṃ śaktitomaravṛṣṭibhiḥ śastraiś ca bahubhī rājañ jaghnatus tāvakān raṇe
english: Then Dhṛṣṭadyumna of the Pāñcālas and the mighty car-warrior Sātyaki, sorely pressing your army with showers of spears and lances and with many weapons, O king, slew your men in the battle.

sanskrit: te hanyamānāḥ samare tāvakāḥ puruṣarṣabha āryāṃ yuddhe matiṃ kṛtvā na tyajanti sma saṃyugam yathotsāhaṃ ca samare jaghnur lokaṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Though slaughtered in the battle, O bull among men, your men, setting their minds on the noble course of war, did not forsake the field; and those mighty car-warriors slew the host in the battle to the full of their valor.

sanskrit: tatrākrando mahān āsīt tāvakānāṃ mahātmanām vadhyatāṃ samare rājan pārṣatena mahātmanā
english: There arose a great cry from your high-souled men, O king, as they were slain in the battle by the great-souled son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ tāvakānāṃ mahārathau vindānuvindāv āvantyau pārṣataṃ patyupasthitau
english: Hearing that dreadful clamor of your men, the two mighty car-warriors Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti turned to face the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: tau tasya turagān hatvā tvaramāṇau mahārathau chādayām āsatur ubhau śaravarṣeṇa pārṣatam
english: Those two mighty car-warriors, slaying his horses in haste, both covered the son of Pṛṣata over with a downpour of arrows.

sanskrit: avaplutyātha pāñcālyo rathāt tūrṇaṃ mahābalaḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ sātyakeḥ sumahātmanaḥ
english: Then the mighty Pāñcāla, leaping swiftly down from his chariot, quickly mounted the chariot of the most great-souled Sātyaki.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā mahatyā senayā vṛtaḥ āvantyau samare kruddhāv abhyayāt sa paraṃtapau
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, surrounded by a great army, advanced in wrath against the two scorchers of foes, the princes of Avanti, in the battle.

sanskrit: tathaiva tava putro 'pi sarvodyogena māriṣa vindānuvindāv āvantyau parivāryopatasthivān
english: Likewise your son too, O sire, with every effort, surrounding Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, took his stand to support them.

sanskrit: arjunaś cāpi saṃkruddhaḥ kṣatriyān kṣatriyarṣabha ayodhayata saṃgrāme vajrapāṇir ivāsurān
english: And Arjuna too, much enraged, O bull among warriors, fought the warriors in the battle as the wielder of the thunderbolt fights the Asuras.

sanskrit: droṇaś ca samare kruddhaḥ putrasya priyakṛt tava vyadhamat sarvapāñcālāṃs tūlarāśim ivānalaḥ
english: And Droṇa, enraged in the battle and doing what was dear to your son, scattered all the Pāñcālas as fire scatters a heap of cotton.

sanskrit: duryodhanapurogās tu putrās tava viśāṃ pate parivārya raṇe bhīṣmaṃ yuyudhuḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: And your sons, with Duryodhana at their head, O lord of the people, surrounding Bhīṣma in the battle, fought against the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā lohitāyati bhāskare abravīt tāvakān sarvāṃs tvaradhvam iti bhārata
english: Then King Duryodhana, as the sun was turning red, said to all your men, "Make haste!" O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yudhyatāṃ tu tathā teṣāṃ kurvatāṃ karma duṣkaram astaṃ girim athārūḍhe naprakāśati bhāskare
english: While they thus fought and wrought deeds hard to do, the sun mounted the western mountain and shone no more.

sanskrit: prāvartata nadī ghorā śoṇitaughataraṅgiṇī gomāyugaṇasaṃkīrṇā kṣaṇena rajanīmukhe
english: In a moment, at the onset of night, there flowed a dreadful river surging with streams of blood, thronged with packs of jackals.

sanskrit: śivābhir aśivābhiś ca ruvadbhir bhairavaṃ ravam ghoram āyodhanaṃ jajñe bhūtasaṃghasamākulam
english: With she-jackals, inauspicious, howling out their fearful cries, the battlefield became dreadful, crowded with hosts of spirits.

sanskrit: rākṣasāś ca piśācāś ca tathānye piśitāśanāḥ samantato vyadṛśyanta śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: And Rākṣasas and Piśācas and other eaters of flesh were seen on every side, by the hundreds and by the thousands.

sanskrit: arjuno 'tha suśarmādīn rājñas tān sapadānugān vijitya pṛtanāmadhye yayau svaśibiraṃ prati
english: Then Arjuna, having vanquished Suśarman and the other kings together with their followers in the midst of the host, returned toward his own camp.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro 'pi kauravyo bhrātṛbhyāṃ sahitas tadā yayau svaśibiraṃ rājā niśāyāṃ senayā vṛtaḥ
english: And Yudhiṣṭhira too, the Kaurava king, then went with his brothers to his own camp by night, surrounded by his army.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'pi rājendra duryodhanamukhān rathān avajitya tataḥ saṃkhye yayau svaśibiraṃ prati
english: And Bhīmasena too, O lord of kings, having conquered in the battle the car-warriors led by Duryodhana, then went toward his own camp.

sanskrit: duryodhano 'pi nṛpatiḥ parivārya mahāraṇe bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ tūrṇaṃ prayātaḥ śibiraṃ prati
english: And King Duryodhana too, having in the great battle surrounded Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu, swiftly set out toward the camp.

sanskrit: droṇo drauṇiḥ kṛpaḥ śalyaḥ kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ parivārya camūṃ sarvāṃ prayayuḥ śibiraṃ prati
english: Droṇa, the son of Droṇa, Kṛpa, Śalya, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvatas, surrounding the whole host, went toward the camp.

sanskrit: tathaiva sātyakī rājan dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ parivārya raṇe yodhān yayatuḥ śibiraṃ prati
english: Likewise Sātyaki, O king, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata, surrounding their warriors in the battle, went toward the camp.

sanskrit: evam ete mahārāja tāvakāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha paryavartanta sahitā niśākāle paraṃtapāḥ
english: Thus, O great king, your men, those scorchers of foes, together with the Pāṇḍavas, withdrew at the hour of night.

sanskrit: tataḥ svaśibiraṃ gatvā pāṇḍavāḥ kuravas tathā nyaviśanta mahārāja pūjayantaḥ parasparam
english: Then, having gone to their own camps, the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus alike settled down, O great king, honoring one another.

sanskrit: rakṣāṃ kṛtvātmanaḥ śūrā nyasya gulmān yathāvidhi apanīya ca śalyāṃs te snātvā ca vividhair jalaiḥ
english: Having made provision for their own safety and posted their pickets in due order, and having drawn out their barbed shafts and bathed in waters of many kinds, those heroes...

sanskrit: kṛtasvastyayanāḥ sarve saṃstūyantaś ca bandibhiḥ gītavāditraśabdena vyakrīḍanta yaśasvinaḥ
english: ...all having had the rites of blessing performed and being praised by the bards, those illustrious ones diverted themselves with the sound of song and instruments.

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva tat sarvam abhavat svargasaṃnibham na hi yuddhakathāṃ kāṃ cit tatra cakrur mahārathāḥ
english: For a while all that was like a glimpse of heaven; for the mighty car-warriors held no talk of battle there at all.

sanskrit: te prasupte bale tatra pariśrāntajane nṛpa hastyaśvabahule rājan prekṣaṇīye babhūvatuḥ
english: And there, O king, while the armies slept and the men were spent with weariness, those two camps, abounding in elephants and horses, became a sight worth beholding.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca pariṇāmya niśāṃ tāṃ tu sukhasuptā janeśvarāḥ kuravaḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva punar yuddhāya niryayuḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When that night had passed and the lords of men had slept in comfort, the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas went forth once more to battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ śabdo mahān āsīt senayor ubhayor api nirgacchamānayoḥ saṃkhye sāgarapratimo mahān
english: Then there was a great din from both the armies as they marched out to battle, vast as the ocean.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā citraseno viviṃśatiḥ bhīṣmaś ca rathināṃ śreṣṭho bhāradvājaś ca vai dvijaḥ
english: Then King Duryodhana, Citrasena, Viviṃśati, and Bhīṣma the foremost of car-warriors, and the brahmin son of Bharadvāja...

sanskrit: ekībhūtāḥ susaṃyattāḥ kauravāṇāṃ mahācamūḥ vyūhāya vidadhū rājan pāṇḍavān prati daṃśitāḥ
english: ...united and well prepared, arrayed the great host of the Kauravas in battle-order and, mailed for war, set it against the Pāṇḍavas, O king.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaḥ kṛtvā mahāvyūhaṃ pitā tava viśāṃ pate sāgarapratimaṃ ghoraṃ vāhanormitaraṅgiṇam
english: Bhīṣma, your father, O lord of the people, formed a great battle-array, dreadful and like the ocean, with its mounts surging like waves.

sanskrit: agrataḥ sarvasainyānāṃ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo yayau mālavair dākṣiṇātyaiś ca āvantyaiś ca samanvitaḥ
english: At the head of all the troops marched Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu, attended by the Mālavas, the Southerners, and the men of Avanti.

sanskrit: tato 'nantaram evāsīd bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān pulindaiḥ pāradaiś caiva tathā kṣudrakamālavaiḥ
english: Next after him came the valiant son of Bharadvāja, with the Pulindas, the Pāradas, and the Kṣudrakas and Mālavas.

sanskrit: droṇād anantaraṃ yatto bhagadattaḥ pratāpavān māgadhaiś ca kaliṅgaiś ca piśācaiś ca viśāṃ pate
english: Next after Droṇa, ready for battle, came the valiant Bhagadatta, with the Māgadhas, the Kaliṅgas, and the Piśācas, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: prāgjyotiṣād anu nṛpaḥ kausalyo 'tha bṛhadbalaḥ mekalais traipuraiś caiva cicchilaiś ca samanvitaḥ
english: After the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa came King Bṛhadbala of Kosala, attended by the Mekalas, the Traipuras, and the Cicchilas.

sanskrit: bṛhadbalāt tataḥ śūras trigartaḥ prasthalādhipaḥ kāmbojair bahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ yavanaiś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: After Bṛhadbala came the brave Trigarta, lord of Prasthala, together with many Kāmbojas and Yavanas by the thousands.

sanskrit: drauṇis tu rabhasaḥ śūras trigartād anu bhārata prayayau siṃhanādena nādayāno dharātalam
english: And the impetuous and brave son of Droṇa, after the Trigarta, O Bhārata, marched forth, making the face of the earth resound with his lion-roar.
